Title: AKU donates academic books to three institutions in Kenya
NewsSummary: Gesture underpins AKU's commitment to partnership and sharing of resources

content.text: As part of its commitment to share knowledge, the Aga Khan University (AKU) has donated 300 academic books to three institutions based in Kenya. The books, previously in the AKU library in Nairobi were donated to the Lamu Port Museum Library, Kenya Medical College (KMTC) Mathari Hospital and the Kenya Technical Teachers College (KTTC), in a gesture that affirmed cooperation and networking with various organisations and the community.

"For libraries to be more impactful, it is important that more collaboration and partnership in information services is emphasised," said AKU Librarian Peter Gatiti said during the event. "One of our core mandates is to empower society with knowledge resources that enhance skills, innovation, decision-making and problem solving."

The Aga Khan University library continually acquires authoritative and the most up to date books in various fields in print and non-print formats to provide users with the best resources. It is an active member of various library networks such as International Federation of Library Associations & Instititutions (IFLA), Kenya Libraries & Information Services Consortium (KLISC), Kenya Library Asscociation (KLA) and Association of Health Information and Libraries in Africa (AHILA), the library advances its partnerships by sharing any extra resources gleaned from within its growing collection.

Appreciating the donation, the Resource Manager for the National Museums of Kenya, Ms Vivienne Nandhoka, who represented Lamu Port Museum Library, also requested more collaboration and partnership with the university and library in areas of research.

The Kenya Medical College (KMTC) Mathari Hospital campus was represented by the librarian, Peter Chagwa, Procurement Officer Purity Kanda and Deputy Principal Mr Joseph Otin. Mr Otin appreciated the book donation on behalf of the institution and thanked the library on behalf of the Principal Ms Florence Maina.

The deputy principal acknowledged the partnership and collaboration between AKU and the College, noting that nine AKU mental health nursing students recently undertook a teaching mentorship program at the college.
KTTC library representative, Mathew Obonyo, also acknowledged the donations and thanked the library for the good gesture. He requested that the institution be considered for future donations.

In his brief remarks, AKU's Regional Librarian, Mr Arnold Mwanzu, thanked the guests for accepting the book donation invitation and emphasised the need for librarians to work together to serve their users better.
